## Methamphetamine use and the Extended amygdala

This next phase of my research is exploring how methamphetamine use impacts the extended amygdala. Building from the imbalance model of addiction proposed by Koob and Volkow (2010), the extended amygdala underpins much of the withdrawal phase, particularly the negative affect associated with it. The theory further posits that this negative affect becomes the primary motivator for substance use as the severity of a substance use disorder increases. Despite this, most neuroimagaing research in people who use methamphetamine have focused on the nucleus accumbens and prefrontal cortex. In a series of studies that I am planning I will explore how methamphetamine use impacts the volume and function of extended amygdala regions as well as the amygdalar-hippocampal circuit which supports memory encoding.

## Methamphetamine use and Trauma

This avenue of research attempts to expand our understand of how previos trauma impacts methamphetamine use.
